subject: Chemistry
title: The Oppau Explosion of 1921
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Oppau Explosion of 1921.

hook.text: In 1921, workers at a BASF plant used dynamite to loosen caked fertilizer. The blast killed 561 people instantly.

buildup.text: A 4,500-ton stockpile of ammonium sulfate and ammonium nitrate had hardened into a solid mass in a silo.

discovery.text: Workers had used small explosive charges to break up caked product 20,000 times before without incident.

twist.text: The composition had shifted to a higher ammonium nitrate ratio. What was routine for one mix became catastrophic for another.

climax.text: The explosion left a crater 90 meters wide and 20 meters deep. Buildings 25 kilometers away lost their windows.

punchline.text: Same procedure, different mixture. A small chemistry change turned routine into disaster.

quiz.question: Why did the Oppau explosion occur after 20,000 safe blasting operations?
options: The fertilizer composition had shifted to a higher ammonium nitrate ratio
The workers used a larger explosive charge than usual
Rain had mixed water with the stored chemicals

details.summary: In 1921 a massive explosion at the BASF fertilizer plant in Oppau, Germany, killed over 500 people when workers used dynamite to break up a hardened pile of ammonium sulfate-nitrate. The blast created a crater 90 meters wide and was heard over 300 kilometers away.
details.whyItMatters: Oppau demonstrated that supposedly stable chemical mixtures can become explosive under certain conditions. It established early precedents for industrial chemical storage safety regulations.
takeaways: Ammonium sulfate-nitrate was considered safe but proved detonable
Workers routinely used small explosives to loosen hardened stockpiles
The blast was one of the largest non-nuclear explosions in history

faq.question: Why did the ammonium sulfate-nitrate explode at Oppau?
faq.answer: The mixture had changed composition over time due to moisture and settling, increasing the proportion of ammonium nitrate. Small blasting charges that previously loosened the pile safely suddenly triggered a full detonation of the more sensitive material.

faq.question: How did the Oppau explosion influence chemical safety practices?
faq.answer: It forced the chemical industry to study detonation sensitivity of fertilizer compounds more rigorously. Storage practices, particularly for ammonium nitrate, were overhauled. However, similar disasters have continued, showing that lessons are often forgotten over generations.
